worrying-early-is-cheap.description: The test of whether a company reaches profitability on its remaining money gives the timeline in which a lag becomes fatal; worrying too early is cheap and worrying too late is dangerous.[1]

default-alive.title: Paul Graham, Default Alive or Default Dead?

revenue-lags-costs.title: Revenue lags costs
revenue-lags-costs.keywords: costs come first, revenue months later, already too late, third time on the board
revenue-lags-costs.script: Remember what the board told us. Costs come first. Revenue comes months later. And by the time you feel that you need sales, it is already too late. The first time you saw the problem. The second time you saw what changes if revenue comes sooner. This time you see what you do about it.

start-now.title: Start now
start-now.keywords: start the pipeline now, revenue before the cash runs out, start when, a few hours each week
start-now.script: So start now. Start the pipeline before you need the money, so that the revenue lands before the cash runs out. The board points back to the first quarter and asks, start when? None of this needs a big budget or a new hire. It needs a few hours of your attention each week, starting now.

four-steps.title: Four steps
four-steps.keywords: zero-cash month, list of potential customers, first contact, deal board, conversion rate and cycle
four-steps.script: Here are the four steps once more. First, build your cashflow view and find your zero-cash month. Second, start a list of potential customers. Third, make first contact. Fourth, put your deals on a board and measure your conversion rate and cycle. None of them needs permission from anyone.

this-week.title: This week
this-week.keywords: pick one step, start this week, put it in your calendar, small version first
this-week.script: Do not try to do all four at once. Pick one step, the one that scares you least, and start it this week. Put it in your calendar now, with a time and a place. When you meet your cashflow board next month, you will be glad you did. Do the small version first. Ten minutes on the board is better than a perfect plan that starts next quarter.
